title: A life as pilgrimage
hookLine: why do pilgrims circle the Kaaba one more time at the very end?
tomorrow: if life is a trip, how much should you pack?

lines: WHY GO BACK AT THE END?
cards: Boarding pass, packed bag, a group text that says landed. Most trips have the same bones: you leave, you get there, you do the thing, you come back. Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, has those bones too, plus one odd detail.
After its biggest day, the standing at Arafat, pilgrims don't simply head home. Before they go, they return to the Kaaba and walk around it once more. Why circle the same House again at the very end?

teach.b: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari gives the rule: the people were told to make their last act the House, a farewell circling before setting out. The trip ends where its center is. Now lay that over a life.
Leaving: pilgrims set out in ihram, two plain white cloths, everything extra left behind. Circling: tawaf, walking around the Kaaba, the center every daily prayer already faces.
Standing: the day at Arafat, hours of standing and asking; in a report in Tirmidhi, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ says Hajj is Arafat.
Returning: and the Qur'an has a line for that, said by Muslims at every loss, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." That's the puzzle solved.

A life read as a pilgrimage keeps coming back to its center, and it ends with a goodbye turn toward it. The Qur'an makes Hajj a duty for those who can find a way there, so not everyone will stand at Arafat.
The shape is open anyway. The same passage on Hajj even says what to pack: "the best provision is to ward off evil." And the surprising bit: the last rite of Hajj is a farewell lap.

how: Muslims who are able make Hajj to Mecca; it includes entering ihram, circling the Kaaba (tawaf), standing at Arafat, and a farewell circling before leaving. Many say 'inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' (Qur'an 2:156) when they hear of a loss.

games.q: what does “a life as pilgrimage” mean?
o: a lifelong plan to visit as many holy sites as possible
the reward earned for each trip taken with good intention
reading your whole life in the shape of Hajj

games.q: the shape of Hajj — tap the pairs.
p: leaving, in two plain white cloths
the day of standing and asking

s: after the standing at Arafat, Hajj is over and pilgrims just go home
a report in Bukhari says their last act is the House: a farewell circling.
the Qur'an makes Hajj a duty for those who can find a way there
it's tied to ability; not everyone will stand at Arafat.
the Qur'an's line for loss says 'unto Him we are returning'
2:156: Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning.

games.q: your friend's grandfather is back from Hajj. he says the hardest moment was the goodbye circle at the Kaaba right before leaving. why does Hajj build in that last lap?
o: so the pilgrim's last act is turning toward the center.
because the day at Arafat doesn't count without it.
it's a later custom, not part of the rules of Hajj.
games.why: the report in Bukhari: people were told to make their last act the House. the trip ends where its center is.

practice: If you can, stand for this one, feet steady, hands open at your sides, the way pilgrims stand at Arafat to ask. Breathe slowly and name, silently, one thing you would ask for if you were standing there.
When you're ready, sit back down.

wordCard.voice: A life as pilgrimage: reading your whole life like Hajj. Leaving what's extra, circling the center, standing to ask, and returning to Allah.

orig.note: Arabic: the pilgrimage to Mecca, a duty for those able to make it.

carryVoice: For the road: a pilgrimage, which ends where its center is. Day one of the journey home.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1755: the people were ordered to make their last act the House (the farewell tawaf), with an exemption for menstruating women

sources.q: Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning.
the best provision is to ward off evil

sources.ref: Qur'an 3:97: pilgrimage to the House is a duty for those who can find a way there
